newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing data -- further details.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing data -- further details.

text.p: Just over half of Britain's manufacturing industries enjoyed increases in production in the three months to April compared with the previous three, the Office for National Statistics said on Monday.
Most notably, output in the coke, mineral oil refining and nuclear fuels industries rose 4.4 percent in the latest three months.

Transport equipment industries saw output rise 2.9 percent while output in both the basic metals and metal products industries and the electrical and optical equipment industries jumped by 1.2 percent.
On the downside, output of machinery and equipment industries fell by 0.9 percent while pulp, paper printing and publishing production dropped 0.6 percent in the latest three months.
Output of electricity, gas and water jumped by 4.5 percent between March and April as near-normal temperatures increased demand.

Within the durable goods industries, output rose by 0.4 percent in the latest three months compared with the previous three. A 2.3 percent fall in car output was offset by a 3.4 percent rise in the output of other durable goods.

In the non-durable goods industries, output rose 0.1 percent in the three months to April. A 1.9 percent fall in clothing and footwear production was just offset by a 0.3 percent rise in food, drink and tobacco and a 0.4 percent increase in other non-durable goods.
Output of the investment goods industries jumped 1.7 percent in the latest three months with electrical goods output up 2.9 percent and transport equipment production up 5.1 percent.
